title: Vulnerable Website
topicTitle: A login check must treat input as data
topicBrief: Websites check usernames and passwords against a database. When an app mixes input directly into the check, input can change what the check means. This old, widely taught problem is SQL injection. This room is only a local mockup — no database exists.
scenario: A fictional company's admin login page does not sanitise its input. Use the one fixed training payload shown by the hints, then inspect the simulated admin page.

tasks.hint1: It is a language applications use with databases.

tasks.prompt: What is the shape of the fixed training input?
tasks.hint1: It uses OR to make a comparison always true.
tasks.hint2: It begins with a quote, then OR, then compares 1 to 1.

tasks.prompt: After the mock login succeeds, inspect the simulated page and submit its flag.
tasks.hint1: Use the Inspect Element button in the mock admin panel.

learn.title: Parameterised queries prevent this
learn.body: When an application mixes untrusted input into a query, the input can alter the query's meaning. Parameterised queries keep the instructions separate from the supplied data, which prevents this class of bug.
